title: Approximate counting of feasible assignments

problem.name: Approximate counting
problem.statement_latex:
For an oracle $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}$, let $a=2^{-n}\sum_x f(x)$. Output $\widehat a$ such that $|\widehat a-a|\leq\epsilon$ with probability at least $2/3$. The count is $2^n\widehat a$; this estimates solution density, feasible volume, or a probability under a reversibly samplable candidate distribution.
The black-box bounds count oracle queries, with gate costs obtained from the reversible oracle; the explicit-CNF comparator counts classical bit operations.

quantum.headline_latex: $O(1/\epsilon)$ queries, quantum counting and amplitude estimation.
quantum.details_latex: For additive error $\epsilon$ and constant failure probability, coherent sampling and its inverse give the stated bound. Relative error $\epsilon a$ for $a>0$ costs $O(1/(\epsilon\sqrt a))$ calls. Gate complexity multiplies these counts by the state-preparation, oracle and reflection costs. The finite domain permits exact enumeration when that is cheaper than the displayed precision-dependent bound.
quantum.headline_text: $O(1/\epsilon)$ queries, quantum counting and amplitude estimation.
quantum.details_text: For additive error $\epsilon$ and constant failure probability, coherent sampling and its inverse give the stated bound. classical.headline_latex: $\Theta(1/\epsilon^2)$ worst-case sampling queries, Monte Carlo estimation.
classical.details_latex: Independent samples give the additive-error bound, capped by $2^n$ evaluations of the entire domain. Relative error costs $O(1/(a\epsilon^2))$ samples. When $f$ is an explicit fixed-width CNF, deterministic tensor contraction computes the count exactly in $\operatorname{poly}(n,m)2^{O(n\log\log n/\sqrt{\log n})}$ bit operations and polynomial space; for $m=O(n)$ the exponent is $O(n/\sqrt{\log n})$. This exact method is an additional comparator at high precision or very small feasible density.

strength.description_latex: Quadratic polynomial improvement in inverse additive precision in the sampling-oracle model, from amplitude estimation. Relative-error improvement also depends on the feasible density $a$.

evidence.description_latex: Tight worst-case sampling-oracle separation in the precision range before finite-domain saturation. Explicit formula structure gives the additional classical comparison stated above.

hardware.description_latex: Small amplitude-estimation circuits have been demonstrated. The input register needs $n$ qubits plus oracle workspace; phase-estimation implementations add $O(\log(1/\epsilon))$ ancillas, while iterative variants reduce this register. Useful high precision requires long coherent oracle sequences and fault tolerance.
